35	// calls their "info" subcommand, and registers them in the agent registry.
36	// Binaries whose name conflicts with an already-registered agent are skipped.
37	// Errors during discovery are logged but do not prevent other agents from loading.
38	// Discovery is skipped when the external_agents setting is not enabled.
39	func DiscoverAndRegister(ctx context.Context) {
40		if !settings.IsExternalAgentsEnabled(ctx) {
41			logging.Debug(ctx, "external agent discovery disabled (external_agents not enabled in settings)")
42			return
43		}

48	// external_agents settings check. Use this in interactive setup flows where
49	// the user explicitly chooses agents.

55	// agent binary matching name. It bypasses the external_agents setting for
56	// explicit, one-invocation selections without executing unrelated plugins.
57	func DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways(ctx context.Context, name types.AgentName) error {
58		return discoverAndRegisterNamed(ctx, name, discoveryTimeout)
59	}
60	
61	// discoveryCanceled reports whether either the caller's context or the derived
62	// discovery-timeout context has been cancelled.
63	//
64	// Both must be consulted. A context closes its own Done channel *before* cancelling
65	// its children, so a goroutine that has just observed the caller's cancellation can
66	// run while the derived context still reports no error — and when the caller is not a
67	// standard context, propagation happens in a watcher goroutine, widening the window
68	// further. Checking only the derived context therefore lets a caller whose deadline
69	// expired mid-operation look like it is still live.
70	func discoveryCanceled(caller, derived context.Context) bool {
71		return caller.Err() != nil || derived.Err() != nil
72	}
73	
74	// discoveryCtxErr wraps whichever of the two contexts has been cancelled, preferring
75	// the caller's, and returns nil when neither has. op names the stage for the message.
76	// See discoveryCanceled for why the caller's context must be consulted too: missing it
77	// lets a caller whose deadline expired mid-lookup receive a nil error and a silently
78	// skipped agent instead of its context error.
79	func discoveryCtxErr(caller, derived context.Context, op string) error {
80		err := caller.Err()
81		if err == nil {
82			err = derived.Err()
83		}
84		if err == nil {
85			return nil
86		}
87		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", op, err)
88	}

91		if name == "" {
92			return nil
93		}
94		if strings.ContainsAny(string(name), `/\`) {

96		}
97		if _, err := agent.Get(name); err == nil {
98			return nil
99		}
100	
101		// `ctx` deliberately stays the CALLER's context; the derived timeout gets its own
102		// name. Shadowing `ctx` with the derived context is what caused the bug this
103		// function is guarding against, and it left the trap in place for the next edit.
104		discoveryCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
105		defer cancel()
106		if err := discoveryCtxErr(ctx, discoveryCtx, fmt.Sprintf("discovering external agent %q", name)); err != nil {
107			return err
108		}
109

112		if ctxErr := discoveryCtxErr(ctx, discoveryCtx, fmt.Sprintf("looking up external agent %q binary %q", name, binName)); ctxErr != nil {
